explanation: Mostly a delimiter-step unit: 88% of activation mass is at the <DEL> step (t == L), where it fires on 51% of sequences. Whether it fires there depends on the first original tokens, i.e. the token about to be output first. Firing rate at <DEL> by first token: w 0.99, n 0.95, e 0.92, r 0.92, z/x/l 0.89, k 0.85, g 0.79, y 0.76, s 0.73, t 0.70, o 0.62, 2 0.58. It is low for i/j (0.08), p/3 (0.12), u, b, a, d, v, f, 1 (0.17-0.27). The second token adds to this: if both of the first two tokens are in the favored set, precision is 0.98, and these cases hold 53% of the mass. A favored second token can make up for an unfavored first one. The largest activations come on <DEL> in sequences starting with w (for example w w ..., w e ...). The other ~12% of mass is weak, scattered firing in the original phase at t >= 3, mostly on the first occurrence of an input token (j, i, 1, a, p are the most common), more often in sequences that start with favored tokens. It is essentially silent at t < 2 and during the copy phase (0.4% of mass). The predicate (<DEL> and one of the first two tokens favored) gets dev F1 0.73 and mass recall 0.875. Weighting the first three tokens raises F1 only to 0.75, so the token-set effect is graded, not a clean rule.
